title: Shadow — Occlusion, Projection, Excluded Capacity and Integration
purpose: Define Shadow as a cross-plane integration/visibility problem rather than a Below realm or synonym for evil, then make it usable across identity, history, culture, institutions and project self-critique.
epistemic_rule: Jungian shadow is a psychological theory/comparator, not a diagnosis tool for named people or groups. Project Shadow is a broader interpretive operator and must not be used to infer hidden motives without evidence.
core_definition: Shadow is content, capacity, history, incentive or contradiction that is excluded from the declared self/model/system and therefore remains poorly integrated or is displaced elsewhere.

shadow_types.meaning: traits/impulses judged unacceptable and therefore disowned
talent, assertiveness, generosity, vocation or realistic insight excluded from conscious identity
events/sources omitted or minimized by the current narrative
incentives, harms, dependencies or contradictions not represented in the institution's official self-description
qualities or anxieties projected onto an out-group rather than recognized within the culture's own dynamics
variables, exceptions or counterexamples excluded from a theory/model because they threaten coherence
Potatoverse material that the project itself under-integrates, overstates or leaves uncorrected

projection.rule: Projection is one possible shadow process, not proof that every criticism reveals the critic's own trait.
projection.evidence_requirement: Do not infer projection from disagreement alone. Look for repeated asymmetry between declared standards and observable treatment of self versus others.
projection.project_use: Useful for examining self-sealing culture, role-lock, enemy production and ideal-vs-practice gaps.

not_meaning: accepting every hidden impulse as authentic
forcing symmetry where evidence is asymmetric
process: differentiate useful capacity from harmful enactment
integration.success_test: Integration should reduce blind repetition and increase accurate self-model, choice, correction and relational capacity.

plane_behavior.heaven-plane: Shadow of ideals: superiority, purity, finality or claimed integration may hide unresolved contradiction, excluded dependence or unacknowledged cost.
plane_behavior.world-plane: Shadow of conduct/institutions: actual incentives and behavior may diverge from public identity.
plane_behavior.below-plane: Shadow of buried history/memory: omitted events, grief, shame, unused capacities or unresolved residue may remain active beneath visible behavior.

findings: Jungian traditions describe shadow as aspects of personality unacceptable to conscious self-image.
Shadow may include positive capacities such as realistic insight, creativity, assertiveness or vocation, not only morally negative tendencies.
Projection is a central way shadow material may be encountered, though projection should not be presumed in every conflict.

relation_to_existing_nodes.swamp: Shadow may feed Swamp when exclusion produces unresolved recurrence, but Shadow can exist without Swamp.
relation_to_existing_nodes.tree_of_strife: Projected/excluded material can become a resource for enemy-production and role-lock, but not every Shadow becomes Strife.
relation_to_existing_nodes.eye: Eye/discernment detects mismatch; Shadow names what the current model fails to integrate.
relation_to_existing_nodes.root: Historical Shadow often lives in buried provenance/memory.
relation_to_existing_nodes.forge: Forge provides bounded processing/testing of shadow material.
relation_to_existing_nodes.fruit: Integration is judged by changed consequences, not by dramatic revelation alone.

boundaries: Shadow is not a demonological category.
Shadow is not hidden motive inference.
Shadow can contain neglected positive capacity.
Collective/institutional shadow requires evidence about systems and behavior, not psychological diagnosis of populations.
